blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules so the function reads without the plan. (1) Replace `if !row.email.is_empty() { ... }` with an early `if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`. (2) Extract the seat loop, duplicated at lines 19-26 and 31-36, into one helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing) -> Result<usize, DbError>` so both branches call it. (3) Name the unexplained filter `seat.contains('@')` (e.g. `fn is_seat_email(seat: &str) -> bool`) or comment why a seat without `@` is skipped silently. (4) Say why seats are only added to an existing account when `account.plan != row.plan`: a reader of line 18 cannot tell whether that condition is the intended rule or a mistake, and would likely assume an existing account on the same plan still gets its new seats. A comment giving the reason, or a well-named guard (`if account.plan == row.plan { continue; }` with its why), answers it. The doc comment on line 11 should also say which seats count (new, email-shaped) so the returned number is not misread.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep, duplicates the seat loop and hides its filters
